claim_verdicts.claim: C4 (snn, surrogate Gauss-Newton H_o = J_sur^T J_sur / n): the dominant/bulk gap is caused by depth, not by data-covariance imbalance
claim_verdicts.evidence: DIRECTION HOLDS: at fixed trace (kappa = 1,10,100,1000, geometric spectrum, trace 16) the SNN's H_o gap statistics after 400 Adam steps are flat in kappa (pooled slopes per decade of log10 kappa: ratio_paper +0.16, ratio_split -0.22, coherence +0.07; log-log exponents |e| <= 0.03; e.g. L=4: coherence 1.79/1.88/2.06/1.93, ratio_paper 5.4/5.7/5.3/6.2), and target imbalance (sv=[1,.1], kappa=1) changes nothing (L=4 end: ratio_split 3.00 vs 2.82, coherence 2.06 vs 1.79). Depth does raise them: at kappa=1 ratio_paper 2.70 -> 5.37 -> 8.21 for L = 2,4,8 (slope 0.89/L, i.e. ~L), coherence 1.25 -> 1.79 -> 3.44 (slope 0.37-0.54/L, log-log exponent 0.73-0.96, i.e. ~0.45 L), ratio_split 1.67 -> 2.82 -> 3.22 (~L^0.5); at kappa=100 the depth slopes are the same (1.06, 0.54, 0.27). Depth-slope / data-slope ratios are >= 5 for every gap statistic. MECHANISM/MAGNITUDE DO NOT: (i) no r^2 = 4 cluster (data-driven dominant count 1.5-4, seed dependent; spectra show no plateau), coherence is ~0.45 L not L; (ii) covariance imbalance does reshape the spectrum: lambda_1 and the bulk edge both grow ~kappa^0.08-0.11 (L=4 end: lambda_1 6.9 -> 10.8, bulk edge 2.3 -> 5.9), so the ratio is flat only because the whole top shifts; (iii) the top-r^2 eigenvectors migrate into W1 as kappa grows (W1 energy L=2: 0.09 -> 0.86; L=4: 0.09 -> 0.49; L=8: 0.03 -> 0.17; at L=2 the readout share drops from 0.91 to 0.14), i.e. the dominant directions become input-covariance directions - the very 'data' mechanism, which deeper nets dilute but do not remove; (iv) the un-normalised 25%x10 condition (kappa=100 but trace 412) collapses coherence to 1.00-1.02 at L=2,4 (1.79 at L=8) with 96-100% of the top-eigenvector energy in W1 and lambda_1 ~ 100-300: a pure data effect that overrides depth (kappa=100 with trace 16 does not do this, so it is the absolute input scale, not the condition number, that matters). Verdict: the paper's statement survives for the SNN only as a statement about trace-normalised condition number and only for H_o.

claim_verdicts.claim: C4 (snn, raw update-field Jacobian H = dg/dtheta of the surrogate gradient, the SNN's actual 'Hessian')
claim_verdicts.evidence: H is exactly block upper-triangular (lower blocks 0 to machine precision in all 72 SNN Hessians), so eig(H) = union of layer-block spectra. After 400 steps the largest real eigenvalue of the raw H equals the readout-block eigenvalue lambda_max(Sigma_a) (uncentred second moment of the rates) exactly, for every L and every condition (L=2: 1.60/1.52/1.30/1.13 for kappa=1/10/100/1000; L=4: 1.04/1.33/0.90/0.87; L=8: 0.62/0.73/0.81/0.55), with d_out = 6 copies (sym(H) dominant count = 6 at L=2,4). lambda_1(sym H) does not grow with depth (1.68 / 1.75 / 1.28 for L = 2/4/8 at kappa=1, vs 2.0 / 6.9 / 7.3 for H_o), coherence of sym(H) saturates (1.05 -> 1.69 -> 2.05), and the kappa dependence enters only through the spike statistics (mean rate 0.29 -> 0.23 at L=2). |H_f|/|H_o| stays 0.90-0.99 at step 400 (asym(H) 1.1-1.2 at L >= 4). The top of the SNN's update-field spectrum is therefore set by a feature-second-moment (data/feature-covariance) mechanism with no explicit depth dependence: neither 'depth' nor input-covariance imbalance in the paper's sense controls it.

Coherence of H_o grows with depth (kappa=1 end: 1.13 -> 1.86 -> 1.93; init 1.16 -> 2.19 -> 4.13 ~ 0.5 L) but also with kappa at L=2 (1.13 -> 1.66) and L=8 (1.93 -> 2.78); ratio_paper grows with depth (0.2-1.0 per L) and, at L=8, with kappa (5.55 -> 7.84 -> 9.07 -> 9.75, +75%; data slope 1.4/decade) but not at L=2 (3.77 -> 3.42); ratio_split shows neither a depth (-0.19..+0.13 per L) nor a kappa dependence (pooled -0.01/decade). W1 energy of the top eigenvectors rises with kappa at L=2 (0.06 -> 0.36). Confound: at L=8 the kappa=1000 nets train further (final loss 0.017 vs 0.056) and lambda_1 falls with kappa (311 -> 137) while it rises at L=2,4. Depth is the more consistent driver, but data imbalance moves the same statistics by comparable amounts in several cells.

claim_verdicts.claim: C4 (linear, gaussian init gain 1, GD) - the paper's claim is derived for balanced init; here it is tested for a generic init as specified
claim_verdicts.evidence: Covariance imbalance raises the gap as strongly as depth does: L=4 end ratio_paper 2.96 -> 3.97 -> 5.34 -> 6.49 for kappa = 1..1000 (+1.2 per decade) vs 1.74 -> 2.96 -> 4.32 for L = 2..8 at kappa=1 (+0.42 per L); ratio_split 6.58 -> 17.5 (+3.3/decade) vs 2.97 -> 10.8 (+1.3/L); lambda_1 20 -> 49 and bulk edge 13.9 -> 28.9 with kappa at L=4 (at init: lambda_1 28.9 -> 73.6, because the W1 block of H_o is (A^T A) kron Sigma_x, verified against the analytic formula). Only the coherence is predominantly depth-driven (2.26 -> 2.63 with kappa at L=4 vs 1.40 -> 2.26 -> 3.70 with L). Target imbalance (sv) has a small effect (ratio_paper 2.96 -> 3.20). Dominant count 2-4.5 (not consistently r^2=4). For a non-balanced linear net the data covariance enters the top of the spectrum directly, so 'depth, not data' does not generalise beyond the balanced-init construction (balanced init: e1/e8).

claim_verdicts.claim: C1 (r^2 dominant + r(d_in+d_out-2r) bulk + zeros) - secondary evidence from this experiment
claim_verdicts.evidence: Data-driven dominant count of H_o (largest log gap): snn 1.5-4 (seed dependent, never consistently 4 across L and kappa), relu 1-6 (6 = d_out at L=2), linear-gaussian 2-4.5; the SNN's sym(H) has exactly d_out = 6 dominant eigenvalues at L=2,4 (readout block I kron Sigma_a, prediction P2). Zero clusters are absent (zero_frac ~ 0 for snn/relu). Covariance imbalance does not create an r^2 cluster either.

SNN H_o ratio_paper (fixed-index definition) ~ L (end: 2.7/5.4/8.2; init 3.1/5.7/10.2 for L=2/4/8) and this is insensitive to kappa, but the data-driven ratio_split is ~1.2 L^0.5 and the coherence ~0.45 L; the fixed-index ratio tracks L mainly because the top of a gap-less spectrum steepens with depth. relu: coherence 0.5 L at init, saturating after training; linear-gaussian: ratio_paper 0.5-1.1 L depending on kappa.

claim_verdicts.claim: C3 (H_f -> 0 under training so H -> H_o) - secondary evidence
claim_verdicts.evidence: snn: |H_f|_F/|H_o|_F = 0.90-0.99 at step 400 for all L and kappa (0.63 at L=2, kappa=1) although the loss fell 50-100x; sym(H) has ~50% negative eigenvalues; asym(H) 1.1-1.2 at L >= 4. Controls hold: relu and linear reach |H_f|/|H_o| <= 0.02 at step 400 (their H and H_o statistics coincide to 2 decimals).

claim_verdicts.claim: C5 (GD preserves balancedness; ratio stays L during training)
claim_verdicts.evidence: No balanced init in this experiment (gaussian/kaiming inits only); only init and step-400 full Hessians were computed.

anomalies: ratio_split (data-driven bulk = eigenvalues between the first and the second largest log gap) is brittle in its lower boundary: e.g. linear L=4, kappa=100, step 400: ratio_split(H_o) = 13.1 vs ratio_split(sym H) = 2.0 although n_dom (4.0), lambda_1 (39.86), coherence (2.60) are identical and |H_f|/|H_o| = 0.01 (the second gap jumped); SNN L=2 sym(H) at kappa=1000 gives 7.8 vs 2.1-3.0 elsewhere. Conclusions therefore rely on coherence, ratio_paper, lambda_1 and the bulk edges (lambda_5 and lambda_{k+1}), which are stable.

The 25%x10 condition changes the input trace (412 vs 16), confounding overall input scale with imbalance (as literally specified): SNN mean rate 0.44, surrogate-window fraction 0.09-0.19, |H_f|/|H_o| at init 4.8-14, lambda_1(H_o) 100-300; all kinds are under-trained after 400 steps (end loss snn 1.07-1.96, relu 0.21-0.46, linear 0.18-0.94 with GD lr capped at 1e-3 - 3e-3). Its 'coherence -> 1 / 100% W1 energy' result is the first-layer block (prop. to Sigma_x) dominating; kappa=100 with trace 16 (k100) does not do this, so it is the absolute input variance, not the condition number, that matters.

Linear GD learning rate deviates from the nominal 0.1: lr = min(0.1, 1/lambda_max(H_init)) as in e2b (0.1 exceeds 2/lambda_max for L >= 4: lambda_max(H_init) ~ 37-250), giving 0.004-0.027 at L=4-8; the L=8 linear nets end at loss 0.005-0.04 (not interpolated). Training progress also differs across kappa for relu at L=8 (loss 0.056 at kappa=1 vs 0.017 at kappa=1000).
H_o at init is identical for kappa=1 and the sv=[1,.1] condition by construction (same X, same init; H_o = J^T J / n does not depend on Y) - the sv condition only differs after training and in H_f.

Library: no bugs found. All cross-checks passed: FD error of H ~1e-9 (snn, relu, linear); linear H_o equals the analytic (A^T A) kron (B Sigma B^T) with the imbalanced Sigma to 1e-10; SNN H has exactly zero lower layer-blocks, so raw eigenvalues were taken as the union of the diagonal-block spectra (validated against dense eigvals to 1e-15 and used for all 72 SNN Hessians); SNN readout block of H equals I_{d_out} kron Sigma_a exactly; local one-eigh statistics match sl.cluster_stats / sl.layer_coherence / sl.top_eigvec_layer_energy to 1e-9.

Operational: the container was restarted (usage limit) after the smoke test had completed (its results/figures were intact) and before the full run was launched; the environment was re-validated with one SNN cross-check and the full run then completed in a single uninterrupted pass (resume logic added to the script but not needed).
reductions: Full surrogate Hessian H only at init and at step 400 (no mid-training full H); H_o every 100 steps (steps 0,100,200,300,400).
400 optimiser steps (as specified by the task) instead of the protocol default 800; final losses are reported per condition.
Smoke test (results/e4_data_imbalance_smoke, 3.7 min): L in {2,3}, seed 0, 40 steps, all 6 conditions and 3 kinds, plus 4 validation cross-checks and an L=8 timing probe.

No conditions, seeds or depths were dropped: all 108 planned runs (3 kinds x 6 conditions x L in {2,4,8} x 2 seeds) completed; budget tiers (seed-1 SNN L=8 last) were never triggered (55.8 min for the runs, 56.5 min with figures/tables).
interpretation: SNN (H_o, the object comparable to the paper's H_o): the gap statistics are depth-driven and kappa-insensitive at fixed trace - depth slopes 0.9/L (ratio_paper), 0.4-0.5/L (coherence), 0.25/L (ratio_split) versus data slopes per decade of kappa of +0.16, +0.07, -0.22 (|log-log exponent| <= 0.03) - so the direction of C4 holds, but with coherence ~0.45 L (not L), no r^2 cluster, the top eigenvalue and bulk edge both scaling ~kappa^0.1, the top eigenvectors moving into W1 with kappa (L=2: 9% -> 86%), and a complete collapse of coherence to 1 when the input scale is not trace-normalised (25%x10). SNN (raw update-field Jacobian): the largest eigenvalue is exactly lambda_max(Sigma_a) of the readout rates (6 copies), independent of depth, so 'depth' is not the cause of the SNN's dominant eigenvalues at all - they come from the readout-feature second moment (the feature-mean mechanism, P2/theory note 5). relu: depth is the more consistent driver but kappa moves coherence (L=2: 1.13 -> 1.66) and ratio_paper (L=8: 5.6 -> 9.8) by comparable amounts; the data-driven gap ratio_split depends on neither. linear (gaussian init): the gap grows with kappa as much as with depth (ratio_paper +1.2/decade vs +0.42/L; ratio_split +3.3/decade vs +1.3/L), only the coherence is depth-dominated; the paper's 'depth, not data' is therefore specific to its balanced-init construction. Verdict on C4 for SNNs: partially - true as a statement about H_o ratios under trace-normalised covariance imbalance (kappa up to 1000), false as a statement about mechanism (no coherent r^2 cluster, eigenvectors relocate to the input layer, absolute input scale dominates) and false for the SNN's actual update-field Jacobian, whose top eigenvalue is a feature-covariance quantity with no depth dependence.
